expectations.text: Identifies SAQ A for card-not-present merchants with all cardholder data functions fully outsourced to PCI-compliant third parties (redirect or compliant iframe)
expectations.evidence: "the applicable SAQ is most likely SAQ A"; "All payment processing and cardholder data handling is fully outsourced to PCI DSS-validated third-party service provider(s)" for CNP redirect/hosted-page merchants

expectations.text: States the merchant's site must not receive/transmit/store cardholder data — only pointing to the payment processor
expectations.evidence: "Your e-commerce site does not itself receive, transmit, process, or store cardholder data — the customer's browser is redirected away"

expectations.text: Notes SAQ A now includes requirements addressing e-commerce skimming risk (script management 6.4.3 and change/tamper detection 11.6.1 style controls)
expectations.evidence: Attributes 6.4.3/11.6.1 to SAQ A-EP only ("SAQ A-EP (with its added script-integrity controls under Req 6.4.3 and change/tamper detection under 11.6.1)"); omits that SAQ A itself now includes skimming-risk requirements

expectations.text: Distinguishes SAQ A-EP: merchants whose site affects the security of the payment redirect (e.g., JavaScript-created payment form) face the much larger SAQ A-EP
expectations.evidence: "SAQ A-EP applies when your site retains some influence over the payment page... embed the payment form via an iframe or JavaScript widget" — larger control set

expectations.text: Advises confirming SAQ eligibility with the acquirer, which determines validation requirements
expectations.evidence: "final SAQ selection should be confirmed with your acquirer, who is the ultimate authority on which SAQ they will accept"
